issue.description:
ADR-005 is Accepted with field evidence (583 assignment-held issues across 47 workspaces, ten starved frontiers, doctor reporting all clean), but no open bead implements the diagnostic. Add a `ready_frontier` check to `doctor` under the `dependencies` scope that warns when `open` issues carry an assignee (these are excluded from the ready frontier but are not active `in_progress` claims), prints a bounded sample of the offending ids, and states the exact remedy: `bead update <id> --clear-assignee`. Advisory only: doctor never clears an assignee, not even under `--repair`. Tests: open+assigned is flagged; in_progress claimants, closed issues, and unassigned open issues are not; the sample is bounded; `doctor --repair` leaves assignment state untouched.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Implement the doctor ready_frontier check for assignment-held issues (ADR-005)

issue.description:
ADR-005 (Accepted) documents the residual gap in its own drawbacks section: 'There is currently no way to mark an assignment as intentionally held', so a workspace that legitimately parks open assigned beads gets the ready_frontier warning on every doctor run, which trains operators to ignore the check. Add an auditable hold marker set through a public CLI mutation — recorded as an audit event, preserved by reopen, serialized through the checkpoint, and covered by unknown-field round-trip conformance — and make the ready_frontier check exempt marked issues while continuing to name ids and the `update --clear-assignee` remedy for unmarked ones. Preserve the ADR's diagnose-don't-mutate posture: doctor never clears an assignee, not even under --repair. The current deferred-status-plus-reservation-note workaround changes lifecycle semantics and is invisible to the check.

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Add an explicit intentional-hold marker so doctor's ready_frontier check can exempt parked assignments
